questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: The map in registers.map: RX_BYTE 0x00, TICK 0x04, STATUS 0x08, REPLY_LEN 0x0C, REPLY_IDX 0x10, REPLY_WORD 0x14, TELEM_LEN 0x18, TELEM_IDX 0x1C, TELEM_WORD 0x20, TAKE 0x24, all 32-bit
questions.reason: The request names these functions but gives no offsets
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)

questions.text: What are the busy bit semantics (STATUS bit 1)?
questions.default: Busy is 1 from the first byte of a packet until its reply is built
questions.reason: The request names the bit but not when it is set
questions.answer: Busy is 1 from the first byte of a packet until its reply is built

questions.text: Does a TICK write while earlier ticks are pending add or restart?
questions.default: A new write replaces the remaining count with n
questions.answer: A new write replaces the remaining count with n

questions.text: What happens to a frame falling due on the same clock as a take write?
questions.default: The take clears the held frame first and the new frame is then held
questions.reason: The request leaves the ordering open
questions.answer: The take clears the held frame first and the new frame is then held
